column3: Hebrew’s final pronoun is singular, “by it”; BSB has plural “by them.”
Hebrew names a young lion and sinning against one’s soul; BSB has a lion and forfeiting life.
Hebrew says ceasing from a quarrel; BSB has resolving a dispute.
Hebrew names winter and asking at harvest; BSB has “in season” and “he looks.”
Hebrew has singular counsel and a singular object of drawing it out; BSB has plural intentions.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew expressly names sons; BSB has the broader children.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “I have purified my heart,” rather than “kept my heart pure.”
Hebrew repeats “stone and stone, ephah and ephah”; BSB interprets differing weights and measures.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew has singular ear and eye; BSB uses plurals.
Hebrew commands being satisfied with bread; BSB predicts having plenty of food.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew calls the lips a precious vessel, not a rare treasure; abundance is explicitly attached to the jewels, not the gold.
The second foreigner is expressly feminine in the printed Hebrew.
Hebrew says “bread of falsehood”; BSB has the broader food gained by fraud.
The first Hebrew clause states plans being established through counsel; BSB makes this a command, “Set plans.”
Hebrew has singular “a secret”; “constant” before gossip is not explicit.
Hebrew joins father and mother with “and”; BSB uses “or.”
Hebrew makes the inheritance’s end the subject of not being blessed.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew retains “stone and stone”; BSB interprets unequal weights.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew explicitly names saying “holy” and has plural vows; BSB has dedicating something rashly.
“Threshing” is not explicit before “wheel” in Hebrew.
Hebrew says “breath” and “all chambers of the belly”; BSB has spirit and inmost being.
Hebrew repeats loving devotion alone as the means of supporting the throne; BSB has “by these,” referring to both devotion and faithfulness.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew explicitly retains the belly’s chambers; BSB has the broader inmost parts. Cleansing in the second clause is supplied from the first.
